title: Separate pots, separate mixes
objectives: Explain why one client can need several different mixes.
List the questions to ask before suggesting any mix.
body_md:
Never apply one mix to all of a client's money. A client can have an emergency fund needed at any time, a house down payment due in three years and retirement twenty-five years away.

## An illustrative client

| Pot | Horizon | Illustrative mix |
|---|---|---|
| Emergency fund | Any time | Cash or liquid 100% |
| House down payment | 3 years | Debt 80% |
| Retirement | 25 years | Equity 70% |

Same client, three mixes. The emergency fund is not there to earn; the house money is not there to take risk; the retirement money is not there to be safe.

## The questions to ask

- "What is this money for, and when will you need it?"
- "If this portfolio fell 25% in a year, what would you do?"
- "How stable is your income? Who depends on it?"
- "Do you have six months of expenses set aside? Any loans?"
- "What else do you own: EPF, PPF, FDs, property, gold?"
- "What did you do during the last big market fall?"

One conversation, several pots, and a target mix for each.
example: Neha, 29, has her wedding fund needed in 18 months invested in a small-cap fund. The fix is not a better fund; it is a separate pot, moved to short-duration debt on a plan.
say: Each pot of money gets its own mix, because each one has its own date.
Your emergency fund is not there to earn returns; it is there to be available.
never: One mix for all your money keeps it simple.
The wedding is two years away; equity will be fine.

check.q: Why does one client need several mixes?
o: Because each pot has its own horizon and job
check.why: Each pot has its own date and job, so each gets its own mix.

check.q: A wedding fund is needed in 18 months. Where should it sit?
o: In short-duration debt or liquid funds
check.why: Money needed that soon belongs in debt or liquid funds, whatever its long-term potential.

check.q: Which question best tests emotional tolerance?
o: If this portfolio fell 25% in a year, what would you do?
How much tax do you pay?
check.why: A concrete loss in rupees, plus past behaviour in a real fall, reveals tolerance.
